title: Husna Bano v. State of U.P. & 9 Others
coram: Ramesh Sinha & Ajit Kumar, JJ. (delivered by Ajit Kumar, J.)
disposition: Writ petition allowed (refusal set aside; application to be reconsidered on the indemnity bond + ID proof)
headnote: A tenant/occupier who cannot obtain the landlord's NOC (here, amid a landlord-tenant and succession dispute) is entitled to a fresh electricity connection on furnishing an Indemnity Bond under Annexure 4.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; proof of possession may be shown by a Ration Card and Aadhaar (rent often being paid in cash, a rent receipt may not exist). The indemnity bond is not a document of title and the grant of a connection does not bar an eviction suit, so a landlord's refusal of NOC is no ground to deny supply. Section 43(1) casts a statutory duty to supply an owner or occupier.

holding_units.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (with s.43(1), Electricity Act 2003)
holding_units.topic: Tenant/occupier's connection on an indemnity bond amid a landlord-tenant dispute
holding_units.question: Can a tenant be denied a fresh connection for want of the landlord's NOC where she has furnished an indemnity bond and proof of possession (Ration Card/Aadhaar)?
holding_units.holding: No. Annexure 4.2 (Clause 4.4) enables an occupier who cannot obtain the owner's NOC to obtain a connection on an indemnity bond; possession can be shown by a Ration Card and Aadhaar (cash rent often leaving no receipt). The bond is not a document of title, and a connection does not bar an eviction suit; the landlord's refusal of NOC is no ground to deny supply. Refusal set aside and remitted for reconsideration.
holding_units.limiting_facts: After the landlady's death, her heirs (in a succession dispute) got the old connection cancelled and refused an NOC; the tenant furnished an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2) plus Ration Card and Aadhaar.

principle_tags.application: A tenant/occupier unable to obtain the owner's NOC may obtain a connection on an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2); the bond is not a title document, and a landlord-tenant/succession dispute is no ground to deny the basic necessity of electricity.

lead_authorities.name: Gaurav Sharma v. State of U.P.

not_decided.note: Possession as tenant or otherwise was treated as a question of fact for the competent civil court; the connection does not bar the pending eviction/injunction suit.

authorities.name: Gaurav Sharma v. State of U.P. & Others
authorities.proposition: A genuine occupier has a statutory right under s.43(1) to a connection and may furnish an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2) where the owner's NOC is unavailable; a family dispute is no ground to refuse. [SCJ-027 in this corpus.]
authorities.how_treated: Followed (its paragraph 9 quoted) as directly governing.

authorities.name: Smt. Sushama Chowdhary v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
authorities.citation: Misc. Bench No. 9588 of 2014 (Allahabad HC, DB)
authorities.proposition: Section 43(1) casts an affirmative duty to supply an owner or occupier; the indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2) covers the case where the occupier cannot produce the owner's consent.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on (through Gaurav Sharma) for the s.43(1) obligation.

authorities.name: Chandu Khamaru v. Smt. Nayan Malik
authorities.proposition: Under Section 43(1), a distribution licensee has a statutory duty to supply an owner or occupier who applies, and a family dispute does not deprive a person of a connection.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on (through Sushama Chowdhary/Gaurav Sharma) for the occupier's statutory right.
